title: Create a Neovim sidebar in Lua
description: The moves that turn an empty buffer into a side panel, using wmti's sidebar as the example. A recipe, one move per step.

steps.title: Make a scratch buffer
steps.why: The panel is UI, not a file, so make an unlisted scratch buffer — nothing the buffer list or :w can grab onto.

steps.title: Mark it throwaway
steps.why: nofile + wipe-on-hide + no-swap tell Neovim never to treat it as a real file to save or recover.

steps.title: Split to the edge
steps.why: botright (or topleft) vsplit drops a new window hard against the right/left edge, full height — the side placement.

steps.title: Fill and size the window
steps.why: Grab the fresh window's handle, drop the scratch buffer into it, and pin the width so it stays a narrow column.

steps.title: Strip the editor chrome
steps.why: Window-local options drop numbers, signs and wrap so it reads as UI; winfixwidth stops other splits from resizing it.

steps.title: Stash the handles
steps.why: Keep the window, buffer and highlight namespace on the session so every later render can find and redraw the panel.

steps.title: Scope keys to the buffer
steps.why: A tiny helper passing buffer=buf scopes every mapping to this buffer, so the panel's keys never shadow your global ones.

steps.title: Wire the keys
steps.why: Bind n/p/Tab/Enter/q to the nav actions — they fire only inside the sidebar, leaving those keys untouched elsewhere.

steps.title: Write the lines
steps.why: Flip modifiable on, replace every line, flip it back off — the panel is redrawn wholesale rather than edited in place.

steps.title: Color it with extmarks
steps.why: Apply per-line highlights through a dedicated namespace, cleared and reapplied each render so styling never piles up.
